claims.statement: integrations/capabilities.toml is a schema_version 2 manifest, and its header requires every integrations/*/ directory to be either declared as an integration or listed in directory_exclusions; the exclusions are cindy, agent-plugin, and opendal, each with a recorded reason.

The directory coverage gate reports directories present but undeclared, declared integrations whose directory is absent, and excluded directories that are absent; it also requires both en and zh integration documentation pages for every integration whose kind is not waived, and lists those pages as evidence for non-unsupported integrations.

documentation_waivers exempts only the evaluation_harness kind from per-host documentation pages, because evaluation harnesses document operation in their own README and the shared evaluation guide; Bub is the declared evaluation harness.

IntegrationCapability is a closed enumeration of 19 identifiers, and its documented contract is that a capability describes user-observable behavior and is never an authorization grant; candidate_review permits listing and reading candidates only and does not imply approval, rejection, or revision authority.

Support profiles are derived, not declared: minimal requires memory_read, memory_write, source_capture, and context_injection; recommended adds work_contract, handoff, acknowledge, and task_outcome; full adds experience_read_or_generate, skill_read_or_generate, candidate_review, and external_skill; an implemented agent_host must declare exactly its derived profiles, and only agent_host integrations may declare profiles or lifecycle.

Implemented integrations (released, master_only, experimental) must declare complete implementation, documentation, and test evidence, at least one toolset, and no proposal or rationale pointer; their declared capabilities must equal the union of capabilities of the tools in their referenced toolsets.

A released integration must declare a release_tag, and the release gate fails when git rev-parse cannot resolve refs/tags/<release_tag>; no declared integration is released at this commit, since no [[integrations]] entry sets availability = "released" or declares a release_tag, and all implemented entries are master_only or experimental.

A proposed integration needs a proposal pointer that is a GitHub issue or pull request URL or an rfcs/ Markdown file, and cannot declare toolsets, profiles, a release tag, or rationale; an unsupported integration needs a docs/ rationale pointer and cannot declare capabilities, profiles, toolsets, or evidence.

Each tool exposure must have either capabilities or a non_profile_reason but not both, tool identifiers must be unique within a toolset, and every declared toolset must be referenced by at least one integration.

Every toolset names a ToolSurfaceProbe; tool_surface_errors runs the probe and reports drift when the probed identifiers differ from the declared tool identifiers, and a probe with no implementation branch raises an unimplemented tool surface probe error.

The server_mcp probe obtains the tool catalog by opening a FastMCP client to the Server's MCP server created with handoff_report_enabled=True, so the declared server-mcp tool list must match the full catalog including opt-in reporting tools.

The json_prompt_hook probe counts a host's UserPromptSubmit or other hook event as complete only when the registered command resolves to a script inside the plugin root and the script contains the required markers; otherwise the event is reported as an incomplete identifier, which the gate treats as drift.

Most tool surface probes verify marker strings or extracted identifiers in checked-in source, such as TypeScript registrations, Python decorators, and YAML provider entries, so a passing probe shows the expected surface is present in source, not that a host executes it at runtime.
For the Codex, Claude Code, WorkBuddy, and ZCode server-mcp integrations, the tool surface gate also requires their packaged .mcp.json to reference both /mcp and powercontext.

A pre-compaction lifecycle has mode unsupported, best_effort, or required_capable; unsupported cannot declare a surface, opt-in, evidence, or pre_compaction_capture, best_effort requires pre_compaction_capture, source_capture, and flush_or_checkpoint plus a surface exposed by a toolset, and required_capable additionally requires an explicit opt-in surface and complete evidence.

At this commit OpenClaw (before_compaction) and Pi (session_before_compact) are the only best_effort pre-compaction integrations, and every other declared agent host is unsupported; no integration uses required_capable.

The manifest declares 16 integrations: 11 agent_host entries (nine master_only hosts Codex, Claude Code, DSH, Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Pi, WorkBuddy, and ZCode, plus experimental kimi-code and minimax), four framework adapters (experimental pydantic-ai and dify, master_only langchain and langgraph), and one evaluation harness (master_only bub).
The minimax integration declares no support profiles although it is experimental, because its declared capabilities omit context_injection, so its derived minimal profile is empty.

render_integration_capability_reference produces an English and a Chinese matrix page with the availability definitions, the profile and pre-compaction explanations, and a table of ID, Kind, Availability, Profiles, Pre-compaction mode, Public surface, and Capabilities for every declared integration.

scripts/generate_integration_manifest_docs.py runs the directory, evidence, release tag, and tool surface gates before rendering and raises without writing any page when a gate fails; it renders one page per DOCUMENTATION_PATHS entry, where en maps to docs/en/docs/integrations/capabilities.md and zh maps to docs/zh/docs/integrations/capabilities.md, and with --check it fails when either checked-in page differs from the rendered output.

The Makefile exposes integration-manifest-docs to regenerate the matrix pages, integration-manifest-docs-check to verify them, and integration-manifest-check to run the docs check and the integration manifest tests; the aggregate check target includes integration-manifest-check.

The generated capability matrix pages at docs/en/docs/integrations/capabilities.md and docs/zh/docs/integrations/capabilities.md must not be hand-edited: they are rewritten by the generator and compared byte-for-byte by the check target and the matrix currency test, and the rendered output carries no in-file generated banner.

integrations/kimi-code/plugins/powercontext/profiles.json is generated by scripts/generate_kimi_profiles.py, which must be rerun when the Server MCP catalog or server-mcp capability assignments change; its --check mode fails when the file is stale, and no Makefile target invokes it.

In the Kimi profile generator, the minimal profile is a fixed three-tool list, recommended and full are computed from server-mcp tools whose capabilities intersect the profile capability set (excluding get_handoff_report), and the full profile adds approve_candidate, reject_candidate, and revise_candidate explicitly.

The HOST_GUIDANCE mapping in guidance.py holds only distribution facts for each host: package roots, recognition source files, and an optional package name; supported capabilities are read from capabilities.toml, not from this mapping.

Guidance refresh owns only the text between the POWERCONTEXT-GUIDANCE START and END markers; malformed or duplicated markers, and unmarked non-empty content, abort the refresh, and every merge is planned before any file is written.

The installers() catalog maps exactly the 11 setup targets, and the matrix test requires that set to equal the set of declared agent_host identifiers, so framework adapters and the evaluation harness are not setup targets.

The pi-tools toolset maps pc_review_approve, pc_review_reject, and pc_review_revise to the candidate_review capability, so the Pi full profile counts candidate decision operations, which contradicts the documented rule that candidate_review never grants decision authority and the server-mcp and Hermes toolsets' non-profile classification of the same operations.

The Codex doctor required-tool list in system.py is hand-maintained with a comment asking maintainers to keep it aligned with capability-bearing server-mcp tools, while the doctor test derives the Codex server-mcp tool set from capabilities.toml and checks that doctor requires each one.

tests/test_cli_capabilities.py tests the Server capabilities command's extraction diagnostic output, not the integration capability matrix; the matrix is covered by tests/test_integration_manifest.py.

The per-integration capability table reproduces the capabilities arrays of the sixteen [[integrations]] entries in integrations/capabilities.toml, in file order, so a reader can see which capability keys each host, framework adapter, and evaluation harness declares.
